phases.Anytime: Studio improvements that need no accounts or services; do them whenever you like
phases.1: Accounts and the first paid publish
phases.3: The expert marketplace, escrow and reviews

done: Image editor with crop and border/frame controls
tasks: A robot clicks through everything on every change. Essential once real money is involved.

Add Playwright tests for all five studio steps (and later sign-up, tasks, payments in Stripe test mode, and publishing), checking for console errors and that screenshots render. Run them with GitHub Actions on every push and before every publish.
The safety net every pro editor has. Nobody fears experimenting.

Add undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and header buttons) using snapshots taken in commit(), grouping fast typing into one step. Add a History panel with save points made automatically every few minutes and before imports, starters and Start over, and let the user restore any of them.
Edit text right on the preview
Double-click a headline in the preview and type. Feels like magic.

In step 3, double-clicking a text box in the preview opens a small floating editor placed exactly over that box (using the box map), editing the matching field. Enter saves, Escape cancels, and the preview refreshes. Keep the Inspector in sync.
Drag and drop for pages, cards and menu links
Sections can already be dragged; this brings it to everything else.

Reuse SortableList to add drag-and-drop reordering for items inside a section (if not already there), pages in the page bar, and menu links and groups in step 4 (including dragging a link into or out of a group), with a keyboard alternative. Keep the existing buttons.
Ctrl+K to jump anywhere or do anything. A power-user favourite.
Add a Ctrl+K command palette: jump to any step, page or section, add a section, switch template, change palette or font. Add a ? shortcut that shows all keyboard shortcuts.
Scores the old site, then shows how much better the new design is. A built-in sales pitch.

After a home page import, add a Site check report in step 1 scoring the old site on readability, colour contrast (WCAG), missing alt text, missing page titles and descriptions, image weight, mobile menu and other clear problems, with plain-language explanations. In step 5, show the same checks for the new design as a before and after comparison. Compute everything in the browser from the import.
Describe your business, get a site
One or two sentences in, a complete draft site out.
Works locally first; an AI server function later

In step 1 Start fresh, add a box: tell us about your business in a sentence or two. Produce name, tagline, pages, sections with real draft copy, palette and font in the project shape, and validate it before applying. Build a smart local version now (keyword-matched starters and copy), designed so an AI server function can replace it later.
Pick a logo and get palettes that match it, with contrast checked.

When a logo is picked (uploaded or from the site), read its main colours on a canvas and offer 3 palettes built from them in step 2. Add a Fix contrast button that nudges any palette to pass WCAG AA, with a pass or fail badge on each palette.
Go beyond 24 templates: any section can borrow a style from any family.

In step 5, after picking a template, let users click a section in the preview to cycle through its layout and style options from every family (hero layouts, card styles, feature styles, video layouts), stored on the section. Add a Shuffle button that proposes a fresh combination. Keep previews as screenshots.
Put 2 or 3 favourites next to each other and decide faster.
In step 5, let users pick 2 or 3 templates to compare on the same page and screen size, side by side with synced scrolling, each with a Use this button.
Every template gets a dark version, plus optional holiday accents.

Add a fourth variant, Dark, for every template family, built automatically from the palette with Art.mix and checked for contrast. Add optional seasonal accent layers (for example winter holidays, summer) that tint bands and buttons.
Events, team, FAQ, pricing, hours, map, logos strip, newsletter.

Add section types: events list, team or staff, FAQ (details and summary), pricing table, opening hours, location with a static map image, logos strip, and newsletter signup. Add importer detection where possible, Inspector fields, and support in all template families and compat rules.
Fresh looks that make the gallery feel endless.

Design 3 new template families clearly different from the current 8, for example an editorial split-screen, an app-style card stack, and a bold pattern-band look using generated SVG patterns. Give each the 3 variants and update the compat rules. Show me thumbnails before publishing.
A full-window walkthrough for pitching a design in a meeting.
Add a Present button in step 5: a full-window, page-by-page walkthrough of the chosen template with device switching, arrow-key navigation, and a final slide with Request development.
Design a site from the couch, not just the desk.
Make the studio itself comfortable on phones and tablets: stacked layouts, bigger touch targets, sticky Back and Next. Make it fully usable by keyboard and screen reader, and check it with axe.
Thumbnails and screenshots that appear almost instantly.

Speed up screenshots: cache converted images and screenshots in IndexedDB so they survive reloads, move heavy work off the main thread where possible, and only render thumbnails that are on screen. Measure before and after and tell me the difference.
New visitors see the studio's power in one click.
Add a short, skippable first-visit tour (about 5 tips) and 3 demo projects (restaurant, community organization, podcast or media) that load in one click.
A bilingual studio and bilingual sites for Canadian clients.
Make the studio bilingual with an English and French switch, with all interface text in one file. Let generated sites have French text per field and a language switch in the menu.
Sign up with a pagename, title and description. The pagename becomes the client's address, email and repository name.

Add Supabase accounts: sign up with pagename (lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, unique, with reserved words like admin and www blocked, and a live availability check), title, description and email login. Roles: client, expert, admin. Save each project to the account with row-level security, keep localStorage as an offline fallback, and move existing local work over on first sign-in. Add a Your projects list to open, duplicate, rename and delete.
pagename@ourdomain for every client, without sharing a Gmail password.
Our email domain set up for forwarding or Google Workspace

Following VISION.md section 6, give each pagename an email address on our domain that forwards to the client's real email with an admin copy. Compare the options (Porkbun email forwarding, Cloudflare Email Routing, Google Workspace, Zoho) by cost, automation and what the client sees. Recommend one.
Each page gets its own GitHub repository in a BAKE organization, created automatically.
A GitHub organization and a GitHub App

Following VISION.md section 6, set up a BAKE GitHub organization and a GitHub App so a Supabase function can create one repository per pagename from a template, turn on GitHub Pages, and later transfer it to the client on request. Walk me through creating the organization and the app step by step.
The engine behind every paid publish: the chosen template becomes a fast, real, standalone site.

Build a site generator that turns a project plus its chosen template into a real static website: every page as an HTML file from render.js, site.css, working menus without screenshots, images copied in, SEO tags, a favicon and a sitemap. Test it on all 24 templates.
The first way to earn: a one-time fee of $25 to $500 depending on the template.

Add paid publishing to <our domain>/<pagename>: set a price tier for each template (from $25 to $500, in one editable file), Stripe Checkout, and then automatically generate the site, push it to the pagename repository and show the live link. Republishing after edits is free. Include a preview of the published URL before payment.
Clients always see what publishing will cost: template tier plus domain option.

Show a live price in step 5: the chosen template's publish tier ($25 to $500), plus +$50 for a new domain or +$100 for an existing domain, plus a typical range for expert help if they've posted tasks. Prices come from one easy-to-edit file shared with checkout.
Terms of service, expert agreement, escrow and refund policy, privacy policy.
A lawyer to review the drafts

Draft plain-language terms of service, an expert agreement, an escrow, dispute and refund policy, and a privacy policy that match VISION.md, as pages in the studio. Mark them as drafts for a lawyer to review.
For $50 more, search, buy and connect a brand-new domain in one flow.
A Porkbun account with API access and prepaid credit

Add the new-domain option (+$50 plus the domain price): search availability and prices with the Porkbun API, register it in the client's name (dry run first, mindful of the $100 per-registration API cap), add the DNS records for GitHub Pages, set the custom domain, and wait for HTTPS to work before telling the client it's live.
For $100 more: a guided, checked setup, with an admin by screen-share as backup.

Add the existing-domain option (+$100): detect the client's registrar from DNS, show exact click-by-click steps for that registrar with the records to copy, check DNS live until it's right, then turn on HTTPS. If the client gets stuck, add them to an admin queue to book a screen-share. Never ask for their registrar password.
Clients keep editing and republish anytime, and can undo a bad publish.
After a site is live, let the client republish changes in one click, see a list of published versions, and roll back to any of them.
Fixes most sites blocking imports, and blocked images in screenshots.

Build a Supabase Edge Function that fetches pages server-side with safety limits (http and https only, no private or local addresses, size, time and rate limits). Importer.fetchHtml tries it first and falls back to Paste code. Also use it as an image proxy so screenshots stop dropping images whose servers block cross-site reading.
Turns the sample artwork tab into real generated logos, heroes and illustrations.
An OpenAI account with billing, plus Supabase

Build a Supabase Edge Function that calls OpenAI image generation with the key kept on the server, a per-user daily limit, results saved to Supabase Storage, and set S.ai.endpoint so the AI images tab uses it.
AI writing help on every field
Improve, shorten, make friendlier, fix spelling or translate any text.
An AI server function (Supabase plus an API key)

Add a small Improve button next to every text field in the Inspector with options: shorter, friendlier, more professional, fix spelling, translate English and French. Show the suggestion with Accept and Try again. Use a Supabase Edge Function with the API key on the server.
Send anyone a link to see the new site on every screen size.

Add a read-only shareable preview link showing the chosen template's screenshots for every page at desktop, tablet and phone, with no editing and no page code. Store the screenshots in Supabase Storage. The owner can turn the link off at any time.
Click any spot and leave a note, like Figma comments. Great for client and expert feedback.

On the shared preview, in step 5 and in task workspaces, let viewers click any spot to leave a pinned comment tied to the box map (section, item or field). Show a comments list with resolve, and include open comments in requests and tasks.
Development requests arrive by email instead of staying in one browser.
Supabase, plus a free email-sending account (like Resend)

Add a requests table in Supabase and send me an email for every new development request, with a snapshot of the project, template, contact details and notes. Show the client a clear confirmation screen and their request status.
Every request or task arrives as a complete brief, so work starts with no back-and-forth.

When a development request or task is submitted, build a clear project brief: pages and sections outline, all copy, chosen images with links, palette and fonts, template, menu settings per screen size, comments and notes. Save it with the request and make it viewable for admins and the hired expert.
Experts show skills, portfolio, rates and reviews, so clients choose with confidence.

Add expert sign-up and public expert profiles: photo, bio, skills, sample work, typical turnaround, languages, and reviews and stats from completed tasks. Add a page where clients can browse and search experts.
Click any part of the preview, describe what you want, and it becomes a task experts can bid on.

Add Ask an expert: the client clicks anywhere in the preview (using the box map) or the studio, writes what they want, and gets a task with a snapshot of their project, screenshots of the marked areas, an optional budget range and a deadline. Tasks appear on a task board for experts.
Turns a vague request into a clear brief and suggests a fair price range.

When a client writes a help request, an AI turns it into a clear brief (what to change, where, and a done-when checklist) and suggests a typical price range based on past tasks. The client edits and confirms it before posting.
Experts quote a price (even $0), a delivery time and an approval window.

Let experts bid on tasks with price (including $0), delivery time, the proposed approval window, and a message. The client compares bids side by side with each expert's reviews, can ask questions, and accepts one, which agrees the approval window.
Chat, files and a safe copy of the client's project for the expert to work on.

Add a task workspace: messages, file attachments, and an expert copy of the client's project the expert can edit without touching the live one. The expert delivers a new version, and the client sees before and after previews and can approve, ask for a revision, or open a dispute. Approved changes merge into the client's project.
The client pays when accepting a quote, and the money is held until they approve.
A Stripe account, plus a quick check with an accountant or lawyer

Plan escrow with Stripe Connect (separate charges and transfers, experts on Express accounts) following VISION.md: charge on accepting a quote, hold until approval, release minus our 10% fee, refunds and partial refunds. Explain the 90-day holding limit, what happens when an approval window runs out, and Canadian compliance questions to ask a professional. Don't build until I approve.
Our 10% fee, expert payouts and clear receipts for everyone.
Add the money pages: the 10% platform fee on every paid task, expert payout history and status, receipts and invoices for clients, and a monthly earnings summary for experts and for us.
An escrow specialist sees everything in one place and decides fairly.

Add a dispute centre for escrow specialists: the brief, bids, messages, every delivered version with before and after screenshots, and the timeline. Actions: release, split or refund, with a written decision sent to both sides and an audit log.
Every finished task gets a public review, so the marketplace earns trust.

After every task, require the client to leave a star rating and a public review before posting their next task or publishing. The expert can reply once. Reviews are marked Verified task and appear on expert profiles.
Completion rate, on-time rate and badges like Rising expert for $0 starters.

Show expert reputation: average rating, tasks completed, on-time rate, repeat clients, disputes, and badges (Rising expert after a few $0 tasks with good reviews, Top rated, Fast delivery). Use them to sort bids.
Keeps payments on the platform and bad actors out.

Add safety features: identity and payout checks through Stripe, rate limits, a warning when messages try to move payment off the platform, report and block buttons, and moderation of public pages and reviews.
Your dashboard for users, requests, tasks, escrow, disputes, domains and manual jobs.

Build an admin-only control room: users and pagenames, development requests with a status pipeline (New, Quoted, In progress, Live), open tasks, money held in escrow, disputes, domain jobs, published sites, and a queue of manual jobs. Every action is logged.
Manual steps get done almost instantly, with alerts to the specialist on call.

Add an on-call system: manual jobs (existing domains, disputes, stuck publishes) go to a queue with response-time targets, an on-call rota, and phone notifications. Clients see live status like Specialist assigned.
Each manual job becomes automatic over time, with the specialist as backup.
Review the manual-job queue and propose which steps to automate next (for example DNS checks, repository setup, HTTPS checks, publish retries), ranked by time saved. Don't build until I choose.
Moves page rendering to a server so nobody can copy your template code.
Possibly a small paid server; plan first

Plan only: compare ways to move Render and Shot to a server (for example Cloudflare Browser Rendering, a small Fly.io headless Chrome service, or a Supabase function) so only images reach the browser. Compare monthly cost, speed and what changes in the studio. Do not build anything until I choose an option.
